Sociedad Química y Minera de Chile S.A. is named as an owner in 2 of the 4 rows; its stated share is 100% in each.

* Commodity: Lithium carbonate — capacity: 44,000 metric tons
* Commodity: Lithium carbonate — capacity: 70,000 metric tons
* Commodity: Lithium hydroxide — capacity: 13500 metric tons

Capacity figures represent facility capacity as of that reporting year, not actual production, and these records name no buyers. In terms of national output, [Chile](/atlas?view=world&country=cl)'s mine production in 2025 was 56,000 t (estimated) (ranking 3rd with a 19.3% world share), according to the [USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026](https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2026/mcs2026-lithium.pdf) (Sourced).

### What is missing: buyers

The buyers of Chile's lithium output are not in our sources. A source that would settle it: offtake and supply agreements disclosed in the producers' annual reports and filings, customs and trade records (UN Comtrade), and the buyers' own procurement disclosures.

Outside the corpus — major commercial purchasers of Chilean lithium products are typically cathode and battery cell manufacturers, as well as automotive OEMs located primarily in China, South Korea, Japan, Europe, and the United States.

You can send primary evidence (such as commercial contracts, trade manifests, or company filings) to get buyer relationships tracked in the corpus.
